findings.summary: Runtime failure skips remaining safe accelerators.
findings.evidence: _distance_with_backend resolves one accelerator and on runtime failure falls directly to pure Python.
findings.impact: Correctness is preserved, but the advertised safe preference order is not fully used after a runtime-only backend failure.
findings.root_cause: Backend selection and backend execution are coupled as a single selected name rather than one per-call execution plan.
acceptance: auto builds one safe ordered execution plan per top-level operation
runtime failure tries the next safe candidate exactly once
pure Python remains the terminal fallback
strict behavior for explicit backend requests remains documented and tested
findings.resolution: One per-call _ExecutionPlan: a runtime failure warns once, drops the failed backend for the rest of the call and tries the next available backend of internal -> rapidfuzz -> python. Tests: test_a_broken_accelerator_warns_once_per_rank_call, test_a_runtime_failure_tries_the_next_safe_backend, test_strict_runtime_failure_still_raises.

findings.summary: rank resolves backend capability for every candidate.
findings.evidence: rank calls _distance_with_backend inside the candidate loop.
findings.impact: Large rankings can repeat metadata/import capability probes and repeated runtime warnings.
findings.root_cause: There is no per-operation resolved backend execution object.
acceptance: rank resolves the execution plan once
one broken accelerator emits at most one warning per top-level rank call
streaming choices and O(limit) top-k behavior remain intact
findings.resolution: rank() builds the _ExecutionPlan once, so the backend is resolved once per call and an unavailable or failing backend warns once per call. Tests: test_rank_resolves_the_backend_once_per_call, test_an_unavailable_backend_warns_once_per_rank_call; streaming and O(limit) tests unchanged.
